 New Jersey State Holidays
 Colleen Petrucci 
 Published Nov 15, 2026 
 New Jersey has 13 state holidays, two more than the federal government, and state offices and the MVC close on every one. Here are the dates for the rest of 2026 and all of 2027, and what is open or closed in South Jersey on each one.
 New Jersey State Holidays in 2026
 The state observes these 13 holidays in 2026, according to the official state holiday list . Two are still to come this year, Thanksgiving on Thursday, November 26, and Christmas on Friday, December 25.

 New Jersey State Holidays in 2027
 The state’s holiday page only lists 2026 so far, but the dates for 2027 follow the fixed rules for state employees set by the New Jersey Civil Service Commission . A holiday that falls on a Saturday is observed on the Friday before, and one that falls on a Sunday is observed on the Monday after. That moves three holidays in 2027.

 New Year’s Day 2028 falls on a Saturday too, so by the same rule state offices close on Friday, December 31, 2027, as well. The 2027 New Jersey holiday calendar below puts every date in one place.
 How New Jersey’s Holidays Differ From Federal Holidays
 New Jersey keeps all 11 federal holidays, though it calls Washington’s Birthday by its common name, Presidents’ Day, and adds two of its own, Good Friday and Election Day. On those two days state offices and the MVC close, while federal offices and the Federal Reserve stay open.
 Juneteenth works a little differently too. The federal holiday is June 19, moved to a weekday when it falls on a weekend, while New Jersey always marks it on the third Friday in June. In 2026 and 2027 the two land on the same day, but in 2028 New Jersey will close on Friday, June 16, and the federal holiday will be Monday, June 19.
 What’s Open and Closed on State Holidays
 State offices and MVC agencies close on all 13 state holidays, so plan errands such as a car inspection around them. Banks follow the Federal Reserve’s holiday calendar , and NJ Transit runs a holiday schedule on 12 days of its own choosing.

 Watch the Fridays before a Saturday holiday. When a federal holiday falls on a Saturday, the Federal Reserve Banks stay open on the Friday before, so banks are usually open on days when state offices are shut. That happened on Friday, July 3, 2026, and in 2027 it applies to Friday, June 18, Friday, December 24, and Friday, December 31. When the holiday falls on a Sunday, banks close on the Monday after, as they will on Monday, July 5, 2027. Individual banks can set their own hours, so check with yours.
 County Offices and Schools in South Jersey
 County governments set their own holiday schedules, and some add days the state doesn’t observe. Cape May County and Salem County both close their offices on the Friday after Thanksgiving, which is November 27 in 2026, even though state offices are open that day. Before you head to a county clerk or surrogate’s office near a holiday, check that county’s schedule.
 Public schools don’t follow the state holiday list. Each school district sets its own calendar, so a district may stay open on a state holiday such as Election Day or close for days the state doesn’t observe.
 Frequently Asked Questions
 Is Election Day a state holiday in New Jersey?
 Yes. State offices and the MVC close on the general election day in November, which is Tuesday, November 2, in 2027. Banks and federal offices stay open, and NJ Transit runs its regular schedule. Polls are open from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., as our guide to when polls open and close in NJ explains.
 Is the MVC closed on state holidays?
 Yes. MVC agencies close on all 13 New Jersey state holidays, including Good Friday and Election Day. They are open on the Friday after Thanksgiving, which isn’t a state holiday.
 Is Good Friday a state holiday in New Jersey?
 Yes. State offices and the MVC close on Good Friday, which falls on March 26 in 2027. It isn’t a federal holiday, so banks and federal offices stay open.
 Is the day after Thanksgiving a state holiday?
 No. State offices and the MVC are open, though some counties, including Cape May and Salem, close their offices, and NJ Transit runs a holiday schedule.
 How many NJ state holidays are there?
 Thirteen. They are the 11 federal holidays plus Good Friday and Election Day.
